user.title: Entity Configuration
user.description: Select the Home Assistant entities to use for power prediction. All three entities must have sufficent statistics available in the recorder.

data_description.integration_name: Custom name for this predictor instance (e.g. 'House', 'Pool', 'EV Charger'). Used to distinguish multiple predictors in the UI. Defaults to 'Power Predictor' if left empty.
data_description.power_entity: The sensor tracking your total power consumption (e.g. sensor.power_consumption). Must have long-term statistics.
data_description.temperature_entity: An outdoor temperature sensor (e.g. sensor.outdoor_temperature). Must have long-term statistics.
data_description.weather_forecast_entity: A weather entity that provides an hourly forecast (e.g. weather.home).

model.title: Model Parameters
model.description: Configure the prediction model. The defaults work well for most setups.

data.peak_start: Peak Period Start Hour (0–23, local time)
data.peak_end: Peak Period End Hour (0–23, local time)

data_description.min_power: Clamp predicted values to at least this value in kW (0 = no minimum beyond zero) Set around you min overnight usage.
data_description.max_power: Clamp predicted values to at most this value in kW. Set just above your typical peak usage.
data_description.history_days: How many days of historical data to train on (1–365).
data_description.update_interval_minutes: How often to retrain and refresh predictions. Minimum 5 minutes.
data_description.n_power_lags: Number of previous hourly power readings to include as features (0 = none = past has no influence on future).
data_description.n_temp_lags: Number of previous hourly temperature readings to include as features (0 = none = past has no influence on future).
data_description.peak_start: Local clock hour when the peak period begins (inclusive). Set this to your real high-usage window — the more conservative Peak Quantile is applied to these hours.
data_description.peak_end: Local clock hour when the peak period ends (inclusive).
data_description.peak_quantile: Quantile applied during peak hours (higher = more conservative / higher predictions).
data_description.offpeak_quantile: Quantile applied during off-peak hours (0.5 = median).
data_description.hour_harmonics: How finely the model can shape the daily curve. 0 = a single straight ramp (old behaviour); 2 forms separate morning and evening peaks; 3 (default) adds finer detail.
data_description.reg_alpha: Overall regularisation strength applied to the standardised features. Higher values smooth the model and make the influence weights below bite harder. 0.1 is a sensible default; higher over-smooths.
data_description.weight_time: Relative influence of time-of-day features. Above 1.0 the daily pattern matters more, below 1.0 less, 0 disables it. Only has an effect when the regularisation strength is non-zero.
data_description.weight_temperature: Relative influence of temperature and its lag features. Lower this if the weather signal is washing out the daily pattern.
data_description.weight_lags: Relative influence of recent power readings (the lag features).
data_description.max_forecast_hours: Maximum hours to forecast into the future (48–168 hours / 2-7 days). Note: Forecasts beyond weather data availability will use historical average temperature.
data_description.hour_offsets: Add a fixed kW offset at a chosen hour of the day, in local time: set the hour (0-23) and the kW to add — e.g. hour 13 adds the offset at 1 pm every day (good for EV charging or a pool pump). Hours not listed are unchanged; offsets may be negative and are still bounded by Min/Max Predicted Power.
